name: Build Muscle, Whole Foods
summary: A week of real home cooking for hard training days, built on potatoes, oats, millet, barley and chickpeas instead of rice or pasta: lighter butter chicken, salmon with romesco, beef stroganoff, Portuguese-style baked cod, chicken adobo and a Saturday turkey meatloaf. Every meal and snack carries protein.
howItWorks:
**Built for training days.** Every breakfast, lunch, dinner and snack carries protein from chicken, turkey, beef, salmon, cod, tuna, eggs, Greek yogurt, cottage cheese and chickpeas, with a big serving at each main meal. Five eating times a day keep a steady supply around your sessions.

**Whole-food carbs for fuel.** Potatoes, sweet potatoes, oats, millet, barley, chickpeas and fruit refill your energy at breakfast, lunch and dinner. There is no rice, pasta or bread in the week: millet goes under the early-week curry and stroganoff, barley into Friday's steak salad, and potatoes, sweet potatoes or oats show up every day.

**Cook once, eat twice.** Monday's butter chicken, Tuesday's salmon, Wednesday's stroganoff, Friday's adobo and Saturday's meatloaf each make two portions, so the next day's lunch is done. The baked cod, the steak salad and Sunday's salmon are cooked fresh.

**Fish and omega-3.** Sockeye salmon on Tuesday and Sunday carries **omega-3 and vitamin D**, with a little ground flax in the oatmeal, smoothie and yogurt bowls. Baked cod on Thursday, canned salmon and a little tuna add more.

**Bigger sizes.** Big grows the proteins (meat, fish, eggs, yogurt, cottage cheese, chickpeas), the starch (potatoes, oats, millet, barley) and a little of the oil, nuts and milk. Vegetables and fruit stay as written, so use a wide pan and a big tray.

recipes.name: Banana bread oatmeal with almonds and Greek yogurt
recipes.about: Creamy stovetop oats simmered with mashed banana, ground flax and cinnamon, so the bowl smells like banana bread. Egg whites are whisked in until it turns thick and custardy, then a cold spoonful of Greek yogurt, toasted almonds and a drizzle of honey go on top. It tastes like a treat and brings **a good hit of protein**.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until they smell nutty, then tip them out.
Bring the milk and an equal amount of water to a gentle simmer in a small pot. Stir in the oats, flax, cinnamon and salt and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Whisk the egg whites in a cup, then stir them into the hot oats in a thin stream. Cook, stirring, for 1 to 2 minutes at a gentle bubble, until the whites turn opaque and firm all the way through.
Stir in the mashed banana for the last minute so it melts into the oats.
Spoon the oatmeal into a bowl and top with the Greek yogurt, almonds and a drizzle of honey.
recipes.tip: Pour the whites in slowly while you stir so they do not clump. Overripe bananas are the sweetest.

recipes.name: Smoky turkey and sweet potato breakfast skillet with spinach and egg
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a classic American breakfast hash
recipes.about: Crumbled turkey, diced sweet potato and peppers browned in smoked paprika, with spinach wilted through and egg cooked in the same pan until completely firm. It is a proper hot breakfast that is **high in protein and vitamin A**, and it all happens in one skillet.
steps: Wash the vegetables. Warm the oil in a wide non-stick pan over medium heat and cook the sweet potato and onion for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sweet potato is tender and starting to brown.

Push the vegetables to the side, add the turkey and break it up. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes until no pink is left and it reaches 74 °C (165 °F). Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw turkey.
Stir in the pepper, garlic, smoked paprika, cumin and salt and cook for 1 minute, then fold in the spinach until it wilts.
Make a gap in the middle. Beat the egg and egg whites together, pour them in and cook, stirring, until completely set and firm, about 2 minutes. Serve straight from the pan.
recipes.tip: Short on time? Cook the turkey and sweet potato the night before while dinner simmers, chill within 1 hour, and reheat them in the pan to 74 °C (165 °F) before you add the egg.

recipes.name: Strawberry yogurt bowl with honey-toasted oats and almonds
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a berry yogurt parfait
recipes.about: Thick Greek yogurt with juicy strawberries and banana, topped with oats and almonds toasted in honey until crunchy. It takes five minutes and gives you **a good hit of protein** before you leave the house.

ingredients.note: thawed in the fridge, or fresh and sliced

steps: Toast the oats and almonds in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until golden. Stir in half the honey and the cinnamon for the last 30 seconds, then tip onto a plate to cool and crisp.
Stir the ground flax into the yogurt, spoon it into a bowl and top with the strawberries, banana and their juice.
Scatter over the crunchy oats and almonds and drizzle with the rest of the honey.
recipes.tip: Toast a few days of oats and almonds at once and keep them in a jar.

recipes.name: Lemon mustard chicken and broccoli stuffed sweet potato with cottage cheese
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by the American stuffed baked potato
recipes.about: A soft baked sweet potato piled with shredded chicken folded into cottage cheese, lemon and a little mustard, with tender broccoli on top. It is sweet, savoury and tangy all at once, and the sweet potato brings **plenty of vitamin A and potassium**.
steps: Scrub the sweet potatoes and wash the broccoli. Prick the sweet potatoes all over with a fork and microwave for about 5 minutes per potato, turning halfway, until a knife slides in easily. For a crisper skin, finish them in a hot oven for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile cover the chicken with water in a small pot, bring to a simmer and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, until it reaches 74 °C (165 °F) and no pink is left. Lift it out, rest for 5 minutes, then shred it. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.
Steam the broccoli for 3 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
Fold the shredded chicken into the cottage cheese with the mustard, lemon juice, parsley, olive oil, salt and pepper.
Split the sweet potatoes, fluff the insides with a fork, and pile on the chicken mix and the broccoli. Warm it for 1 minute in the microwave if you like it hot.
recipes.tip: For a packed lunch, carry the chicken mix and the sweet potatoes separately in a cold bag with an ice pack, eat the same day, and assemble when you sit down.

recipes.name: Seared steak and warm barley salad with lemon mustard dressing
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a steak house plate and warm grain salads
recipes.about: Thin slices of seared sirloin on a bowl of chewy barley, chickpeas, sweet grated carrot and tender broccoli, all tossed in a sharp dressing of olive oil, lemon, yellow mustard and parsley. It is a steak house plate turned into a hearty lunch. The beef brings **iron and zinc**, and the barley and chickpeas bring fibre.
steps: Wash the vegetables. Rinse the barley and simmer it in plenty of water for 25 to 30 minutes, adding the broccoli for the last 3 minutes. Drain well and let it steam dry for a few minutes. Spread any you are not using right away in a shallow container and chill within 1 hour.

Pat the beef dry and season it with the pepper and a pinch of salt. Sear it in a very hot pan with a little of the oil for 3 minutes a side until browned, then turn the heat to medium and keep turning it every minute until it reaches 71 °C (160 °F) in the middle, then rest it on a clean plate for 5 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after handling it raw.
Whisk the mustard with the lemon juice, the rest of the oil, parsley and the rest of the salt. Let the onion sit in the dressing for 5 minutes to soften.
Toss the warm barley and broccoli with the chickpeas, dressing and carrot. Slice the steak against the grain, lay it on top, and pour over any resting juices.
recipes.tip: Cook the barley on Thursday evening while the cod bakes (cool it within 1 hour and chill), and this lunch takes about 15 minutes. Packing it? Keep the steak and salad in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat them the same day.

recipes.name: Lighter butter chicken with chickpeas and spinach over cumin millet
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Punjabi butter chicken, lightened with yogurt and chickpeas
recipes.about: Tender chicken simmered in a silky tomato sauce with garam masala, ginger and garlic, thickened with Greek yogurt instead of cream. Chickpeas and spinach soak up the sauce, and fluffy cumin millet takes the place of rice. It makes two portions, and **tastes even better the next day**.
steps: Wash the spinach. Rinse the millet and toast it in a dry pot for 2 minutes with the cumin seeds. Add two and a half times its volume of water, cover and simmer for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed. Rest 5 minutes and fluff. Cool what you are saving in a shallow container within 1 hour.
Toss the chicken with half the yogurt, the turmeric, paprika and half the garam masala. Leave it to marinate in the fridge while you start the sauce.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 6 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the tomato paste for another minute.

Add the crushed tomatoes and salt and simmer for 8 minutes. Stir in the chicken and chickpeas, cover and cook for 10 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F). Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then the rest of the yogurt and the remaining garam masala so the yogurt does not split.
Serve over the cumin millet. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch: cool within 1 hour, refrigerate, and reheat until steaming hot, to 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: To freeze, cool the curry within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C. Freeze it without the millet.

recipes.name: Pan-roasted sockeye salmon with romesco, crispy potatoes and broccoli
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Catalan romesco with roasted fish
recipes.about: Seared sockeye salmon with golden roasted potatoes and tender broccoli, finished with a quick romesco of roasted pepper, tomato and almonds. The sauce is smoky, tangy and a little sweet. The salmon is a rich source of **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and it makes a second plate for tomorrow's lunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 230 °C (450 °F) and wash the vegetables. Toss the potatoes with half the oil and a pinch of the salt on a large tray (use two trays if they crowd, so they crisp instead of steam), and put the pepper halves cut side down on another tray. Roast the potatoes for 25 minutes, turning once, and the pepper for 15 to 20 minutes, until blistered and soft. Toast the almonds alongside for the last 4 minutes.
Blitz the roasted pepper, almonds, crushed tomato, half the garlic, smoked paprika, vinegar, a spoonful of the oil and a pinch of the salt into a thick, rustic sauce.

Pat the salmon dry and season with a little salt. Sear it in a hot non-stick pan with the rest of the oil, skin side down if it has skin, for 4 minutes, flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes more until it reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Rest it on a clean plate. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Steam the broccoli with the remaining garlic for 4 minutes, until bright and tender, then dress it with the lemon juice.

Serve the salmon on the potatoes with the broccoli, a spoonful of romesco and the parsley. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch: cool within 1 hour, refrigerate, and reheat until steaming hot, to 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Fresh salmon is cooked the day you buy it, or bought frozen and thawed in the fridge. Spoon leftover romesco onto potatoes or eggs; it keeps covered in the fridge for 3 days.

recipes.name: Beef stroganoff with mushrooms over millet
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Russian beef stroganoff and millet kasha
recipes.about: Strips of lean sirloin seared hot, then simmered with mushrooms, onion and paprika in a silky sauce finished with Greek yogurt in place of sour cream. It sits on fluffy millet, a nod to Russian kasha. It makes two portions and **reheats beautifully**.
steps: Wash the mushrooms and onion. Rinse the millet and toast it in a dry pot for 2 minutes. Add two and a half times its volume of water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer for 15 minutes, then rest 5 minutes and fluff. Cool what you are saving within 1 hour.

Pat the beef dry and season it with the pepper. Sear it in a hot pan with half the oil in two batches, 1 to 2 minutes a side, then move it to a clean plate. Wash your hands and the board after handling it raw.

Lower the heat, add the rest of the oil and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until they have given up their water and browned. Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the soy sauce and a good splash of water and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, until the sauce coats a spoon.

Return the beef and its juices to the pan and warm through until the beef reaches 71 °C (160 °F). Take the pan off the heat and stir in the yogurt, mustard and half the dill. Do not boil it again or the yogurt will split.
Spoon over the millet and finish with the rest of the dill. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch: cool within 1 hour, refrigerate, and reheat gently until steaming hot, to 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Reheat the leftovers gently, on low, stirring: the yogurt sauce can split if it boils hard.

recipes.name: Portuguese-style baked cod with sliced potatoes, peppers, onion and parsley
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Portuguese bacalhau no forno and bacalhau com grão, made with fresh cod
recipes.about: Thick cod fillets baked over thinly sliced potatoes, chickpeas, sweet red pepper and onion with garlic, smoked paprika and a little tomato, then finished with a handful of parsley and lemon. It is a one-tray dinner with **plenty of lean protein**, inspired by the Portuguese way with salt cod, potatoes and chickpeas.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F) and wash the vegetables. Toss the potatoes, onion, pepper, garlic, chickpeas, smoked paprika, salt and most of the oil in a large baking dish or on a tray (use two trays if they crowd, so they roast instead of steam). Roast for 18 to 20 minutes, turning once, until the potatoes are just tender at the edges.
Pat the cod dry and season it with pepper. Spoon the crushed tomato over the vegetables, nestle the cod on top and drizzle with the rest of the oil.
Bake for 12 to 14 minutes, until the fish flakes and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Finish with the lemon juice and the parsley.
recipes.tip: Cod is cooked the day it is bought, or thawed overnight in the fridge. Haddock or pollock work the same way.

recipes.name: Chicken adobo with crispy potatoes and garlicky green beans
recipes.about: The Filipino national dish: chicken braised in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic and bay until the sauce is tangy, salty and a little sweet. Crispy roasted potatoes catch the sauce, as they do in many Filipino homes, and quick green beans keep it fresh. It makes two portions, and the flavour **deepens overnight**.
steps: Heat the oven to 230 °C (450 °F) and wash the vegetables. Toss the potatoes with a little of the oil on a tray (use two trays if they crowd, so they crisp instead of steam) and roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Warm the rest of the oil in a wide pan and brown the chicken for 3 to 4 minutes a side, then move it to a clean plate. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.

Add the onion and most of the garlic to the pan for 2 minutes. Pour in the soy sauce, vinegar, honey, bay leaf, pepper and the same amount of water as soy sauce and vinegar together, and bring to a boil, scraping up the browned bits.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, until it reaches 74 °C (165 °F). Take the lid off and simmer for 4 to 5 minutes more, until the sauce is a glossy glaze.
Steam the green beans with the last of the garlic for 5 minutes until bright and tender.
Serve the chicken and sauce with the potatoes and green beans. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch: cool within 1 hour, refrigerate, and reheat until steaming hot, to 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Use the vinegar you have; cane, coconut or plain white all work. Reduce the sauce a few minutes longer for a thicker glaze.

recipes.name: Turkey and oat meatloaf with garlic sweet potato mash and broccoli
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by the classic North American meatloaf
recipes.about: A juicy turkey meatloaf bound with oats and grated carrot, glazed with a sticky tomato and honey topping and served with creamy garlic sweet potato mash. It is Saturday dinner comfort food with **a big hit of protein**, and it makes a second plate for tomorrow's lunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F) and wash the vegetables. Mix the turkey with the oats, egg whites, carrot, onion, half the garlic, parsley, most of the salt and the pepper, using your hands, until just combined. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw turkey.
Shape it into a loaf on a lined tray and wash your hands again. Stir the tomato paste, honey and vinegar into a glaze and brush it over the top.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes, until the loaf reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the middle. Rest it for 10 minutes before slicing.

Meanwhile boil the sweet potato in salted water for 12 to 15 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Drain, saving a splash of the cooking water. Return to the pot with the olive oil, the remaining garlic, a pinch of salt and enough of the water to loosen it, and mash until fluffy.
Steam the broccoli for 4 minutes until bright and tender.
Serve slices of the loaf with the mash and broccoli. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch: cool within 1 hour, refrigerate, and reheat until steaming hot, to 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Leftover slices reheat well in the oven or a pan, covered, until steaming hot, to 74 °C (165 °F).

recipes.name: Baked sockeye salmon with parsley salsa verde, green beans and crisp potatoes
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian salsa verde with baked fish
recipes.about: Sockeye salmon baked until just flaky and spooned over with a sharp, herby salsa verde of parsley, lemon, garlic and a little mustard, with golden potatoes and green beans. It is a simple one-tray plate, and the salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F) and wash the vegetables. Toss the potatoes with a third of the oil and a pinch of the salt on a large tray (use two trays if they crowd, so they crisp instead of steam) and roast for 20 minutes, turning once.

Pat the salmon dry, rub with a little oil, salt and pepper, and add it to the tray. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until it reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and the potatoes are golden. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Chop the parsley and garlic finely and stir them into the rest of the oil with the lemon juice and zest, mustard and pepper for the salsa verde.
Steam the green beans for 5 minutes until bright and tender.
Serve the salmon with the potatoes and green beans and a big spoonful of the salsa verde.
recipes.tip: Fresh salmon is cooked the day you buy it, or bought frozen and thawed in the fridge.

recipes.name: Banana berry yogurt smoothie with flax and milk
recipes.about: A thick, cold smoothie blended from Greek yogurt, milk, banana, frozen strawberries and ground flax. It drinks like a milkshake but is built from whole foods, with **a good hit of protein** in the glass.
steps: Put the milk, yogurt, banana, strawberries, flax and cinnamon in a blender.
Blend for 1 minute until completely smooth and thick. Add a splash of milk if it is too thick to pour.
recipes.tip: Freeze the banana in chunks for an even thicker, colder smoothie.

recipes.name: Cottage cheese with apple, honey and toasted almonds
recipes.about: Creamy cottage cheese topped with juicy apple, a drizzle of honey and crunchy toasted almonds. A simple bowl with **a good hit of protein** that tastes like a treat.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant.
Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl and top with the diced apple and almonds, then drizzle with the honey.

recipes.name: Paprika deviled eggs with red pepper strips
recipes.about: Firm-boiled eggs filled with a creamy mix of yolk, olive oil, lemon and a little mustard, dusted with smoky paprika and served with sweet red pepper strips. It is a classic party snack with **protein and choline**.

ingredients.note: boiled until the yolks are firm

steps: Lower the eggs into boiling water and simmer for 10 minutes, so the yolks are completely firm. Cool in cold water and peel.
Halve the eggs, scoop the yolks into a bowl and mash with the olive oil, mustard, lemon juice and pepper until smooth.
Spoon the filling back into the whites and dust with paprika. Serve with the red pepper strips. Keep chilled, put any left over back in the fridge within 2 hours, and eat within 3 days.

recipes.name: Apple slices with a peanut butter cottage cheese dip
recipes.about: Crisp apple slices with a creamy dip of peanut butter blended into cottage cheese with a pinch of cinnamon. Sweet, salty and filling, with **protein from the cottage cheese and peanuts**.

ingredients.note: to keep the apple from browning

steps: Blend or whisk the peanut butter, cottage cheese and cinnamon until smooth.
Toss the apple slices with the lemon juice and serve with the dip.

recipes.name: Tuna, caper and parsley stuffed pepper boats
recipes.about: Sweet red pepper halves piled with a creamy mix of tuna, cottage cheese, capers, parsley and lemon. A crunchy no-cook snack with **lots of lean protein**.
steps: Mix the tuna with the cottage cheese, capers, parsley, lemon juice, olive oil and pepper.
Spoon the mix into the pepper boats. Tip any leftover tuna into a covered container, chill it and use it within 2 days.

recipes.name: Lemon dill chicken bites with a cucumber yogurt dip
recipes.about: Little cubes of chicken breast seared with lemon, garlic and paprika, served with a cool dip of Greek yogurt, grated cucumber and dill. They are warm, juicy and packed with **a good hit of protein** for very few calories.
steps: Toss the chicken with half the lemon juice, half the garlic, the paprika and the pepper.
Sear the chicken in a hot non-stick pan with the oil for 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until golden and 74 °C (165 °F) in the middle. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.

Mix the yogurt with the cucumber, dill, the rest of the lemon juice and garlic, and the salt. Serve the warm bites with the dip. Chill any leftovers within 2 hours and eat them within 3 days, cold or reheated to 74 °C (165 °F).

recipes.name: Carrot, pepper and spinach egg white frittata bites
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Spanish tortilla and American egg muffins
recipes.about: Fluffy baked bites of whisked egg whites with grated carrot, spinach, red pepper and dill, set until completely firm. They are savoury, filling and easy to eat on the move, with **a good hit of protein** from egg whites and very little fat.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F) and grease as many cups of a muffin tin as you need with a little of the oil.
Cook the carrot and onion in a small pan with the rest of the oil and a splash of water for 4 to 5 minutes, until the carrot is just tender. Stir in the pepper and spinach until the spinach wilts.
Whisk the egg whites with the dill, salt and pepper, and stir in the vegetables. Divide among the muffin cups, filling each about three-quarters full.

Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until the bites are puffed, golden, completely firm and 74 °C (165 °F) in the middle. Cool and chill within 2 hours, and eat within 3 days, cold or reheated to 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Make a batch of 6 or more bites on Sunday and eat them cold or warmed through. Do not freeze them.

recipes.name: Canned salmon and lemon parsley cucumber rounds
recipes.about: Flaked canned salmon mixed with a little cottage cheese, lemon, parsley and mustard, piled onto crisp cucumber rounds. A fridge-cold snack with **omega-3 and calcium from the soft salmon bones**.
steps: Flake the salmon in a bowl, mashing the soft bones in well. Mix in the cottage cheese, parsley, lemon juice, mustard and pepper.
Wash the cucumber, cut it into thick rounds and pile the mix on top. Tip any leftover salmon into a covered container, chill it and use it within 2 days.
